Although the 61% increase in VAV reheat load for the VAV HEDS relative to the alternate CAV-VAV hybrid baseline is unexpected, it is a result of the heating energy being supplied mostly from the high fan power in the alternate CAV baseline case. 26 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Figure 14 shows a comparison between the load metrics for the original CAV baseline and alternate CAV-VAV hybrid baseline cases, while Figure 15 shows the metrics for the VAV baseline and VAV alternate baseline cases. The cooling coil water side load is included in these figures to point out the large quantity of energy that is wasted in both measured baseline cases. Turning off the cooling coil when the net load requirement is heating results in very large energy reductions. When cooling is required, the basic strategy employed in the alternate baseline cases still results in some VAV reheat, but the net effect is a strong reduction in the overall VAV reheat load between the original and alternate baseline cases. The alternate CAV-VAV hybrid baseline required only 7.3 kW average VAV reheat load vs. a value of 86.9 kW in the original CAV baseline, representing a reduction of 91.5%. The corresponding values were 22.8 and 53.9 kW for the alternate VAV baseline and original VAV baseline cases, respectively, representing a reduction of 57.7%. Since there are more periods requiring cooling in the VAV baseline, this resulted in additional VAV reheat in the alternate VAV baseline case. Additionally, since the air flow rate is already reduced in the VAV operation, the alternate VAV baseline does not have the same magnitude reduction in the cooling load as does the CAV baseline case, according to Eq.
